# [Baseline] - WIN - D - Shared PC

Puts shared Windows PCs in Shared PC mode with Entra accounts only: profiles of users who have not signed in for 30 days, or when free disk space drops below 25%, are removed, there is no local storage outside the profile and maintenance runs at 02:00.

| | |
|---|---|
| Platform | Windows |
| Scope | Device (D) — assign to device groups |
| Type | Device config |
| Assignment | — |
| Source | Own baseline — Intune Shared multi-user device (sharedPCConfiguration, SharedPC CSP). OpenIntuneBaseline deliberately does not cover shared devices (WINDOWS/README.md). |
| File | [`Baseline_WIN_D_Shared_PC.json`](Baseline_WIN_D_Shared_PC.json) |

> Own group SG-D-UEM-WIN-SharedPC (assigned), next to SEC-Shared-Devices: a shared device is in SEC-Shared-Devices (WHfB Multi User, Wireless Shared Devices) and in exactly one of SG-D-UEM-WIN-SharedPC or SG-D-UEM-WIN-SharedPC-Guest. Two Shared PC policies on one device result in a Conflict in Intune, and then neither does anything. Shared PC mode only affects new sign-ins: profiles that already existed before the policy landed are not always cleaned up by the account manager — preferably start with a clean device (Autopilot reset). A user's profile disappears after 30 days of inactivity or as soon as free space drops below 25%; above 50% free space profiles are kept. That is why OneDrive with Known Folder Move should be on for these devices, otherwise files disappear with the profile. `disableEduPolicies` is set to true: the education settings of Shared PC (including no Store apps, no Cortana) do not belong here. Combine with [Baseline] - WIN - D - Windows Hello for Business Multi User, so that not every new user is taken through PIN setup at first sign-in.
